extraction_notes.note: The paper disables five blocks with \begin {comment} (with a space) under \excludeversion{comment}; latex_facts.py did not strip them, so Theorem posfuncded, Proposition monsuprel, Theorem onedimext, Proposition rksc and Problem 29 appear as facts (and shift the printed numbering).

The disabled comment blocks (facts F6, F7, F8, F38, F43, F54 and their surrounding prose, including the ice-cream cone example) are not printed in the paper and were not extracted; the figure figrdpex is only described through its caption, which was not extracted.

Two \ref typos: the proof of Theorem suprtc says 'under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{suprt}', and the proof of Proposition suprtrdpf cites 'Lemma~\ref{suprtrdpf}' where Lemma suprtlf0 is meant. Both are marked as mentions; a uses edge LP2->PP22 records the intended lemma.

Section 3 says its arguments are 'mostly based on' Aliprantis-Tourky with direct references omitted; only the Riesz-Kantorovich transform definition was marked external, the numbered propositions with proofs were kept as origin paper.

Hahn-Banach Theorem (superlinear-minorant form) is presented as a 'natural extension of a well-known result' without citation and with a proof sketch; marked external standard rather than a paper contribution.

Single sentences ('Combining this with Proposition rkass leads to ...', 'This leads to the Riesz-Kantorovich theorem ... as soon as one notices ...') were taken as prose proofs of Proposition onlysing and the cited Riesz-Kantorovich Theorem.

Step rule 7 requires nesting the 'Let us verify the converse inequality' claim, but step rule 4 would merge its single introduction sentence into the next one and leave one child; the two children were kept separate.
The open problem is restated in a rephrased form at the start of the last section; it is kept as one node from the introduction.

Suppose that $X$ and $Y$ are ordered linear spaces, $X_+$ is a generating cone in $X$,
$Y$ is a Dedekind complete lattice and $\mathcal L$ is a linear space of operators from $X$ to $Y$
satisfying $\rlinop {X} {Y} \subset \mathcal L \subset \blinop {X} {Y}$.
Suppose also that either the following assumptions is satisfied.
\begin {enumerate}
\item
$Y = \mathbb R$; we set $X_r = X_+$ in this case.
\item
$\mathrm{int} X_+ \neq \emptyset$ and $Y$ is Archimedean; we set $X_r = \{0\} \cup \mathrm{int} X_+$ in this case.
\end {enumerate}
Then the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin {enumerate}
\item
$\mathcal L$ is a lattice.
\item
$\mathcal L$ has the Riesz Decomposition Property.
\item
The Riesz-Kantorovich transform $\rkts {T}$ of any finite collection~$T$ of operators from $\mathcal L$ is linear on $X_r$.
\item
For any operator $T \in \mathcal L$ the Riesz-Kantorovich transform $\rktps {T}$ is linear on $X_r$.
\item
$X$ ordered by the cone $X_r$ has the $\mathcal L$-Riesz Decomposition Property.
\end {enumerate}
Moreover, if any (and therefore all) of these conditions are satisfied then $\mathcal L = \rlinop {X} {Y}$
and $\sup T = \rkts {T}$ in $\mathcal L$ on $X_r$ for any finite collection of operators $T \subset \mathcal L$.
